papers.title: Beyond AlphaFold 3: a standardised benchmark of open-source co-folding models for antibody-antigen complexes, from docking accuracy to interaction specificity.
papers.abstract: Co-folding models are increasingly used to predict antibody-antigen complexes for epitope mapping, candidate triage and structure-guided de novo design or engineering, yet the latest generation of these models has not been compared under standardized conditions. We benchmark AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast and OpenDDE on 200 test-set complexes (121 Fvs and 79 VHHs) from SAbDab2-Bench, a newly curated dataset, and a reconstructed antibody-antigen subset of FoldBench, Ab-FoldBench. Using standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics that isolate the antibody-antigen inte
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks five open-source co-folding models (AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast, and OpenDDE) on antibody-antigen complex prediction using a newly curated dataset of 200 complexes (SAbDab2-Bench) plus a reconstructed FoldBench antibody subset. It evaluates docking accuracy and interaction specificity under standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics, providing a fair comparison of the latest generation of co-folding tools for antibody-antigen modeling.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Insight into Softening Mechanism of Zirconia and Prediction of Removal Depth in Magnetic Abrasive Finishing.
papers.abstract: Zirconia ceramic is widely used in dentistry and precision industries owing to its high hardness and fracture toughness. Nevertheless, its high hardness and toughness cause severe tool wear, and microcracks tend to form on the machined surface during conventional mechanical processing. This paper proposes a NaOH-PVP-deionized water composite system to realize green chemical softening of zirconia at room temperature and atmospheric pressure. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that OH- forms strong chemical bonds with surface Zr atoms, thereby inducing surface hydroxylation and increasing the
papers.summary: This paper proposes a NaOH-PVP-water chemical system that softens zirconia ceramic surfaces at room temperature and pressure, making the material easier to machine. Molecular dynamics simulations show that hydroxide ions bond to surface zirconium atoms, hydroxylating the surface and weakening it, and the authors use this to predict removal depth during magnetic abrasive finishing.

papers.title: Computational and Experimental Studies of PSMA-Targeted Conjugates Designed for Subcellular Delivery of Theranostic Radiometals to Prostate Cancer Cells.
papers.abstract: Background: The membrane receptor prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a validated target for theranostic radioconjugates in the treatment and imaging of prostate cancer (PCa). Radioconjugates targeted at PSMA rely mostly on the peptidomimetic glutamate-urea-lysine (Glu-urea-Lys) binding motif to facilitate tumor accumulation. The combination of this binding motif with subcellular targeting moieties, such as acridine orange (AO) and triphenylphosphonium (TPP) derivatives, for nuclear and mitochondrial delivery, respectively, might open the way to innovative dual-target approaches. This
papers.summary: This study computationally designed and experimentally tested PSMA-targeted conjugates that combine the Glu-urea-Lys binding motif with subcellular-targeting moieties—acridine orange for nuclear delivery and triphenylphosphonium for mitochondrial delivery—to direct theranostic radiometals to specific organelles in prostate cancer cells. The work explores a dual-targeting strategy that could enhance the efficacy of PSMA-based radioconjugates for imaging and therapy.

papers.title: Computational Structural and Dynamic Insights into the Proposed TcP21-CXCR4 Interaction: A Consensus-Based Multireplica Simulation Approach.
papers.abstract: Chagas disease, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, is a neglected tropical disease with limited therapeutic options, underscoring the need for novel targeted strategies. The parasite's secreted 21 kDa virulence factor, TcP21, promotes extracellular amastigote host-cell invasion and persistence by interacting with the human chemokine receptor CXCR4, a class A G protein-coupled receptor. Despite its biological importance, the structural determinants governing TcP21-CXCR4 complex formation remain unknown. To elucidate the molecular basis of this host-parasite recognition, multiple initial candidate bin
papers.summary: This study uses consensus-based multireplica molecular dynamics simulations to model the proposed interaction between the Trypanosoma cruzi virulence factor TcP21 and the human chemokine receptor CXCR4. The authors identify candidate binding poses and structural determinants that may govern host-parasite recognition, providing a computational foundation for understanding how TcP21 promotes parasite invasion. The work is purely computational and offers hypotheses rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrated Toxicological, Network Toxicology, and Molecular Simulation Assessment of Inhalation Toxicity and Mechanisms of HFO-1336mzz(E) as an SF6 Alternative Insulating Gas.
papers.abstract: HFO-1336mzz-(E) is a novel environmentally friendly insulating gas with a low global warming potential and favorable dielectric properties, and it has been regarded as an important potential substitute for sulfur hexafluoride (SF6). However, its systemic toxicological characteristics and underlying mechanisms under inhalation exposure remain insufficiently investigated. To address this issue, the present study, for the first time, systematically evaluated the biological safety of HFO-1336mzz-(E) by integrating multilevel toxicological assessment with molecular mechanistic analysis. Acute inhal
papers.summary: This study provides the first systematic safety evaluation of HFO-1336mzz(E), an environmentally friendly insulating gas proposed as a replacement for SF6, using integrated toxicological assays, network toxicology, and molecular simulation. The authors characterize acute inhalation toxicity and propose molecular mechanisms underlying any observed effects. The work supports the biological safety profile of this gas as an SF6 alternative.

papers.title: Investigating Ferritin Permeability to Metal-Based Drugs through Molecular Dynamics.
papers.abstract: In this study, we implemented a workflow based on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to assess whether gold-(I)-containing complexes can traverse the C3 channels of human H ferritin and which energetic barriers were at play in the process. By using two example complexes for which an extensive experimental characterization was already available, we observed that classical MD correctly indicated which one could spontaneously pass through the channel. To quantify the ability of the ferritin nanocage to retain the internalized complex, we estimated, through steered MD and umbrella sampling simula
papers.summary: This study used molecular dynamics simulations to test whether gold-based drug complexes can pass through the C3 channels of human H ferritin, a protein cage that could serve as a drug delivery vehicle. Classical MD correctly predicted which of two experimentally characterized complexes could spontaneously traverse the channel, and steered MD with umbrella sampling quantified the energetic barriers and the cage's ability to retain the internalized drug. The work provides a computational workflow for assessing ferritin permeability to metal-based therapeutics.

papers.title: Solving the Computational Peptide Design Puzzle: Challenges and Opportunities.
papers.abstract: Peptides are increasingly recognized as promising therapeutics, antimicrobial agents, and supramolecular biomaterials due to the remarkable versatility encoded in their amino acid sequences. However, the rational design of peptides remains challenging because sequence-structure-function relationships are not yet fully understood. Experimental exploration of peptide chemical space is inherently limited by the vast number of possible sequences and the complexity of resolving peptide behavior at molecular resolution. Computational methods, particularly molecular dynamics simulations and, more rec
papers.summary: This review discusses the challenges and opportunities in computational peptide design, emphasizing that the vast sequence space and incomplete understanding of sequence-structure-function relationships make rational design difficult. It highlights molecular dynamics simulations and emerging machine learning approaches as key tools for navigating peptide chemical space and accelerating the discovery of peptide therapeutics, antimicrobials, and biomaterials.

papers.title: Toll-Like Receptors in Mycoplasma Infections: Immunopathogenesis, Cheminformatics, and Machine Learning-Based Insights into TLR-Targeted Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma species are the minimal-genome pathogens that elicit complex host immune responses involving both protective and pathogenic inflammation. Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are pivotal components of the immune system, recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and damage-associated molecular patterns to initiate immune responses. TLRs recognize Mycoplasma-derived lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA motifs, initiating NF-κB and MAPK signaling cascades. While these pathways are indispensable for microbial clearance, their dysregulation contributes to chronic inflammation, auto
papers.summary: This review examines how Toll-like receptors recognize Mycoplasma components such as lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA, triggering NF-κB and MAPK signaling that can both clear infection and drive chronic inflammatory pathology. The authors combine immunopathogenesis discussion with cheminformatics and machine-learning approaches to identify potential TLR-targeted therapeutics. It is a broad synthesis aimed at connecting mechanistic immunology with computational drug-discovery strategies for Mycoplasma infections.

papers.title: Structural Characterization of Mycobacterium tuberculosis IspQ Reveals Membrane-Dependent Stabilization of Its Conserved Electron-Transfer Cofactor Network.
papers.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis persistence in granulomas depends on lipid catabolism through the β-oxidation-coupled respiratory pathway, which requires the essential membrane-associated protein IspQ, encoded by Rv0338c. Although IspQ is a genetically and chemically validated drug target, its structural organization and membrane-dependent function remain unknown. Using AlphaFold3 structure prediction, cofactor mapping, evolutionary conservation analysis, and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we show that IspQ adopts an EtfD-like fold containing four iron-sulfur clusters, a heme b, and a me
papers.summary: The authors used AlphaFold3 structure prediction, cofactor mapping, conservation analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the structure of Mycobacterium tuberculosis IspQ, an essential membrane-associated protein required for lipid catabolism during infection. They show that IspQ adopts an EtfD-like fold containing four iron-sulfur clusters, a heme b, and a menaquinone-binding site, and that its electron-transfer cofactor network is stabilized by membrane association. This provides structural insight into a validated drug target whose organization was previously unknown.

papers.title: Theoretical Calculations of CO2/CH4 Separation through Windowed Carbon Nanotube Membranes.
papers.abstract: Distinct topological features endow windowed carbon nanotube (CNT) membranes with great potential as molecular sieves for efficient gas separation and purification. In this work, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were adopted to systematically investigate the CO2/CH4 selective separation performance of such membranes. Key structural and operational parameters, including CNT diameter, pressure, initial feed gas molar ratio, and nanowindow density, were modulated to comprehensively evaluate the molecular sieving capacity toward CO2 and CH4. Simulation results reveal that heteroatom-functionali
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate how windowed carbon nanotube membranes separate CO2 from CH4, varying nanotube diameter, pressure, feed gas ratio, and nanowindow density. The results show that heteroatom functionalization and structural parameters strongly influence molecular sieving performance, suggesting these membranes could be tuned for efficient gas separation.

papers.title: Bridging traditional knowledge and modern technology: In-silico ethnopharmacology in herbal drug discovery.
papers.abstract: The use of herbal medicines and phytochemicals has gained considerable attention due to their structural diversity, selective toxicity, lower incidence of adverse effects, and affordability compared to conventional chemotherapy. Nevertheless, their precise mechanisms of action and bioactive constituents remain insufficiently understood, limiting their clinical translation and highlighting the need for rigorous scientific investigation. This review provides an integrative perspective on herbal-based drug discovery, beginning with the intersection of traditional disease classification systems, s
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
papers.summary: This review discusses how computational (in-silico) methods can be combined with traditional ethnopharmacological knowledge to accelerate herbal drug discovery. It covers the intersection of traditional disease classification with modern computational approaches, aiming to clarify mechanisms of action and identify bioactive phytochemicals. The work is a broad integrative overview rather than a primary research study.

papers.title: Multiscale computational modeling of circulating tumor cells: From separation and detection to targeted drug delivery.
papers.abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) provide a minimally invasive window into cancer progression and metastatic dissemination; however, their extreme rarity, phenotypic heterogeneity, and mechanical adaptability make their isolation, identification, and therapeutic targeting challenging. Although computational methods have been applied to individual steps of CTC research, the field lacks a unified framework connecting molecular recognition, cell mechanics, microfluidic separation, detection, vascular transport, and targeted drug delivery. This review addresses that gap by organizing computational ap
papers.summary: This review proposes a unified multiscale computational framework that connects the disparate steps of circulating tumor cell (CTC) research—molecular recognition, cell mechanics, microfluidic separation, detection, vascular transport, and targeted drug delivery—into a single organizing structure. It argues that although computational methods exist for individual stages, no integrated framework currently links them, and it surveys modeling approaches across these scales to address CTC rarity, heterogeneity, and mechanical adaptability.

papers.title: Why Computational Predictions Fall Short in Subclass B1 Metallo-β-Lactamase Inhibitor Discovery: Progress, Pitfalls, and Translational Opportunities.
papers.abstract: The global dissemination of subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs), especially New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase-1 (NDM-1), Verona integron-encoded metallo-β-lactamase-2 (VIM-2), and imipenemase-1 (IMP-1), threatens the clinical utility of carbapenems and other β-lactam antibiotics. This challenge is compounded by the absence of any commercially available MBL inhibitors for clinical use, underscoring the urgent need for novel inhibitor development. Computational approaches now guide much of MBL inhibitor discovery, yet many compounds predicted to bind B1 MBLs, or even shown to inhibit purified en
papers.summary: This review examines why computational methods for discovering subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamase inhibitors (targeting NDM-1, VIM-2, IMP-1) often fail to translate into clinical candidates, despite guiding much of current inhibitor discovery. It catalogs progress in computational screening alongside common pitfalls—such as poor correlation between predicted binding and actual inhibition of purified enzymes—and outlines opportunities to improve translational success. The central message is that computational predictions alone are insufficient and must be better integrated with experimental validation.

papers.title: In silico antigenic and vaccinological characterization of two production-optimized recombinant yellow fever virus envelope proteins.
papers.abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) remains a major public health threat in Africa and South America. Although the live-attenuated 17D vaccine is highly effective, its use is restricted in certain vulnerable populations, emphasizing the need for nonreplicating alternatives. We performed an integrated in silico characterization of two production-optimized recombinant YFV envelope (Env) proteins derived from the Asibi and 17D strains. Physicochemical, antigenicity, solubility, allergenicity, epitope conservation, structural modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD), electrostatic, and immune sim
papers.summary: This study uses computational (in silico) methods to characterize two recombinant yellow fever virus envelope proteins derived from the Asibi and 17D strains, assessing their physicochemical properties, antigenicity, solubility, allergenicity, epitope conservation, and structural dynamics. The work supports the development of nonreplicating subunit vaccine candidates as alternatives to the live-attenuated 17D vaccine, which is restricted in vulnerable populations. The findings are preliminary and computational, requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Fast and Slow Motions Drive Elusive Polymorphic Transitions in a Naphthalene-Diimide Crystal.
papers.abstract: Thermally induced solid-state polymorphic transitions in an n-hexyl-functionalized naphthalene-diimide organic semiconductor (NDI-C6) are investigated using atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. NDI-C6 exhibits two stable polymorphs: the α phase at room temperature and the γ phase at higher temperatures. The MD simulations reproduce the structural stability of both phases and provide a refined description of their unit-cell parameters and side-chain conformations, which have been only partially resolved experimentally. The α-to-γ transition proceeds through a sequential, nonconcerted
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.summary: This study uses atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how a naphthalene-diimide organic semiconductor crystal transitions between two stable polymorphs (α at room temperature, γ at high temperature). The simulations reproduce both phases and refine their unit-cell parameters and side-chain conformations, which were only partially resolved experimentally. The α-to-γ transition is found to proceed through a sequential, nonconcerted mechanism involving both fast and slow molecular motions.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics-Informed Prediction of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Partitioning into Phospholipid Bilayer Environments.
papers.abstract: The incredible diversity of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) creates a difficult challenge for predicting the steady-state partition ratios indicative of cellular health and function. Many PFAS are amphiphilic surfactants, often with ionic or polar headgroups driving their aqueous solubility and nonpolar tails driving the molecules to interfacial environments. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations generate potential of mean force (PMF) curves that integrate the energy of molecular interactions along a defined pathway, offering a means to understand how PFAS interact with and pass throu
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to compute potential of mean force (PMF) profiles for diverse PFAS molecules crossing phospholipid bilayers, providing a physics-based route to predict their membrane partition ratios. The approach links PFAS amphiphilic structure (polar headgroup plus fluorinated tail) to interfacial and transmembrane energetics, offering a computational alternative to costly experimental partitioning measurements for the vast PFAS chemical space.

papers.title: AlphaFold-based structural analysis of the Treponema pallidum proteome provides a clearer prediction of the organism's biological and pathogenic attributes.
papers.abstract: Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum (TPA), an obligate bacterial pathogen that causes the sexually transmitted disease syphilis, is an extreme auxotroph with a minimal genome and distinct parasitic lifestyle. Approximately 17% of its 977 annotated proteins lack a predicted function because they show little sequence similarity to proteins of known function from other organisms. We therefore utilized the robust structural modeling and matching capabilities of AlphaFold and FoldSeek to create a whole-proteome atlas for the Nichols type strain of this bacterium (TPANIC), with the goal of providing
papers.summary: The authors used AlphaFold protein structure prediction combined with FoldSeek structural matching to build a whole-proteome structural atlas of the syphilis pathogen Treponema pallidum Nichols strain. This approach allowed them to assign likely functions to previously uncharacterized proteins, including roughly 17% of the 977 annotated proteins that lacked functional annotation based on sequence alone. The atlas provides structural insights that clarify the organism's biology and pathogenic mechanisms.

papers.title: Machine Learning with Iterative Error-Driven Refinement for Predicting PFAS-Coated Surface Wettability.
papers.abstract: PFAS coatings impart strong water and oil repellency on materials, but their environmental persistence necessitates sustainable alternatives. The development of alternative chemistries is hindered by limited mechanistic understanding of how molecular structure and surface organization govern intrinsic water and oil wettability. Here, a machine learning-driven molecular dynamics (MD) simulation framework was developed to predict and rationalize the intrinsic water and oil wettability of PFAS coatings on nylon for both water and oil. By systematically sampling PFAS head group types (-CHO, -COOH,
papers.summary: The authors developed a machine learning framework combined with molecular dynamics simulations to predict how different PFAS coating chemistries on nylon affect water and oil repellency. By iteratively refining predictions based on errors, the approach aims to speed up the discovery of sustainable alternatives to persistent PFAS coatings. The study focuses on understanding how molecular structure and surface organization control wettability.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Graphene and Graphene-Derived Ionic Liquid Supercapacitors: A Review of Methods and Applications.
papers.abstract: Graphene and graphene-derived electrodes combined with ionic liquid electrolytes provide atomically well-defined, high-surface-area interfaces and wide electrochemical windows, making them benchmark platforms for supercapacitor research. Understanding how molecular-scale structure at this interface controls macroscopic capacitance requires molecular dynamics simulation since neither continuum theory nor experiment alone resolves the relevant length and time scales. This review treats the electrode-charging methods availablefixed and constant-charge, constant potential, electronic-structure-aw
papers.summary: This review surveys molecular dynamics simulation methods for modeling graphene and graphene-derived ionic liquid supercapacitors, focusing on how electrode-charging schemes (fixed/constant charge, constant potential, and electronic-structure-aware approaches) affect predictions of interfacial structure and capacitance. It argues that molecular-scale simulation is essential because continuum theory and experiment alone cannot resolve the length and time scales governing capacitance. The paper serves as a methodological reference for computational electrochemistry at carbon-ionic liquid interfaces.

papers.title: Strong light-matter coupling as a photonic substituent: cavity-induced electronic and structural control of regioselectivity in nitrobenzene.
papers.abstract: Strong coupling to the vacuum electromagnetic field of optical cavities has been proposed as a route to control ground-state chemical reactivity, enabling "photonic substituent effects." Recent theoretical work predicted that cavity coupling can invert intrinsic regioselectivity in electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. Here, we revisit this prediction using correlated ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics. Using cavity-constrained QED-DFT geometry relaxations followed by QED-CCSD(2,2) calculations of the Wheland intermediates, we confirm substantial energetic reordering and p
papers.summary: This study uses correlated ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics to test whether strong light-matter coupling can act as a 'photonic substituent' that alters ground-state chemical reactivity. The authors confirm that cavity coupling substantially reorders the energies of Wheland intermediates in nitrobenzene, supporting the prediction that it can invert intrinsic regioselectivity in electrophilic aromatic substitution. The work provides a rigorous quantum-chemical validation of cavity-induced electronic and structural control over reaction selectivity.

papers.title: Discovery of novel small-molecule binders targeting IL-6 receptor conformational ensembles to regulate IL-6 signaling.
papers.abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) signaling via its receptor (IL-6R) is a central driver of inflammation and immune-related diseases. Although monoclonal antibodies targeting this pathway are clinically effective, their limitations, including high costs and parenteral administration, create an urgent need for orally available small-molecule inhibitors. However, targeting the extensive protein‒protein interaction interface between IL-6 and IL-6R remains a significant challenge.
papers.summary: This study identifies novel small-molecule compounds that bind to different conformational states of the IL-6 receptor, aiming to block IL-6 signaling as an alternative to antibody-based therapies. The work addresses the challenge of targeting a large protein-protein interaction interface and suggests a path toward orally available inhibitors for inflammatory and immune-related diseases.

papers.title: Characterization of Clonixeril as a Positive Modulator of DMXAA-Induced Murine STING Signaling.
papers.abstract: Stimulator of Interferon Genes (STING) is a central mediator of innate immune signaling and a therapeutic target for inflammatory diseases. Previously, we identified Clonixeril (CXL) as a concentration-dependent inhibitory modulator of human STING (hSTING) signaling. Despite structural conservation, murine STING (mSTING) and hSTING differ in ligand recognition and activation. We posit that CXL may exhibit distinct activity in the murine system. Mice are used in biomedical research due to their genetic similarities to humans and their utility in evaluating systemic activity and safety of therap
papers.summary: The authors characterize Clonixeril (CXL), previously identified as an inhibitor of human STING signaling, and find that in the murine system it instead acts as a positive modulator of DMXAA-induced murine STING signaling. This species-specific divergence highlights differences in ligand recognition and activation between mouse and human STING, with implications for using mouse models to evaluate STING-targeted therapeutics.

papers.title: Novel EGCG Analog Modulates Host Immune Response to Promote Intracellular Clearance of Staphylococcus Aureus Through Interaction With the 67-kDa Laminin Receptor.
papers.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (SAB) is a leading cause of sepsis. Intracellular bacterial survival in liver macrophages contributes to persistent bacteremia. We evaluated the immunometabolic action of EGCG epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), a green tea polyphenol, and its synthetic analogs (MCC-2 and MCC-4) and the putative target, 67-kDa laminin receptor (67LR).
papers.summary: This study investigates how EGCG, a green tea polyphenol, and its synthetic analogs (MCC-2 and MCC-4) modulate the host immune response to clear intracellular Staphylococcus aureus, a major cause of persistent bacteremia and sepsis. The authors identify the 67-kDa laminin receptor (67LR) as a putative target mediating these immunometabolic effects in liver macrophages. The work suggests that EGCG analogs could be developed as host-directed therapeutics to combat intracellular bacterial persistence.

papers.title: Handshake: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction at scale using ProstT5 and cross-chain attention.
papers.abstract: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction, identifying which residues of a protein form the interface when bound to a specific partner, remains a challenging task with significant implications for drug discovery and understanding of protein structure and function. Existing computational methods are limited by small training datasets, inconsistent redundancy filtering, and reliance on three-dimensional structural information at test time. Here we present a sequence-only, partner-specific protein-protein interface predictor called HandShake. It combines ProstT5, a protein language
papers.summary: HandShake is a new computational tool that predicts which amino acid residues on a protein will form the binding interface with a specific partner protein, using only sequence information. It combines the ProstT5 protein language model with cross-chain attention to capture partner-specific interactions, addressing limitations of prior methods that required 3D structures or suffered from small, inconsistently filtered training data. This enables scalable, structure-free prediction of protein-protein binding sites with potential applications in drug discovery and protein function annotation.

papers.title: Computational Discovery of Plant-Derived Peptides with Therapeutic Potential: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Computational methods are increasingly applied to the discovery of plant-derived peptides, but the extent, composition and reporting practice of this literature have not been mapped. Following PRISMA-ScR and Joanna Briggs Institute guidance, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect and PubMed were searched for records published between 2021 and 2026. Of 5062 unique records, 593 were screened at title and abstract, 88 full texts were assessed, 80 sources met all five eligibility criteria and 79 were charted. Overall, 49 (62.0%) were primary studies, 12 (15.2%) described a tool or database and 18 (
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the literature on computational discovery of plant-derived peptides with therapeutic potential, screening over 5000 records and charting 79 sources published between 2021 and 2026. It finds that most work consists of primary studies, with a smaller share describing tools or databases, and highlights gaps in reporting practice across the field. The review provides a structured overview of methods, scope, and evidence quality in this emerging area.

papers.title: An OGE-HPLC-ABTS-Q-TOF MS Screening of Antioxidant Components in Gushuning Tablet (GSN) With Computational Prediction of Related Biological Targets.
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is a severe skeletal disorder that poses a major threat to public health, and oxidative stress may be one of its core pathological mechanisms. The Traditional Chinese Medicine compound preparation Gushuning Tablet (GSN) has been reported to show potential clinical benefits in OP, potentially related to the modulation of OP-associated oxidative stress. However, its antioxidant active material basis and mechanism of action remain unclear. This study aimed to establish an online gradient extraction (OGE)-high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)-2,2'-azinobis-(3-ethylbenzthi
papers.summary: This study combines online gradient extraction HPLC with an ABTS antioxidant assay and Q-TOF mass spectrometry to screen and identify antioxidant compounds in the traditional Chinese medicine Gushuning Tablet, a preparation used for osteoporosis. The identified compounds were then analyzed with computational target prediction to suggest biological pathways through which they might act against oxidative stress in osteoporosis. The work provides a chemical and mechanistic basis for the tablet's reported clinical benefits.

papers.title: Identification and structural characterization of MMP1 and MMP9 as potential targets of curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a major subtype of lung cancer characterized by substantial molecular heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Curcumin and resveratrol are naturally occurring bioactive compounds with reported anticancer activities, but their potential molecular targets and mechanisms in LUAD remain incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses computational approaches to identify matrix metalloproteinases MMP1 and MMP9 as potential molecular targets of the natural compounds curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma, and characterizes the structural basis of these interactions. The work suggests a possible mechanistic link between these dietary polyphenols and suppression of MMP-mediated tumor invasion, though experimental validation is limited.

papers.title: Structure-based computational screening of cyclotides as putative CYP19A1-binding scaffolds for modulation of estrogen biosynthesis in adenomyosis.
papers.abstract: Adenomyosis is a chronic estrogen-dependent gynecological disorder associated with dysmenorrhea, abnormal uterine bleeding, chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and recurrent implantation failure. Because human placental aromatase cytochrome P450 (CYP19A1) plays a central role in local estrogen biosynthesis, this study employed an integrated in silico workflow to identify cyclotide scaffolds capable of interacting with CYP19A1. The receptor structure was prepared and validated, while protein-protein interaction analysis confirmed its involvement in steroidogenesis and estrogen biosynthesis. Twent
papers.summary: This study used computational docking and molecular dynamics to screen cyclotide peptides as potential binders of the aromatase enzyme CYP19A1, which drives local estrogen production in adenomyosis. The authors identify candidate cyclotide scaffolds that may interact with the enzyme's active site, proposing them as starting points for developing estrogen-modulating therapeutics. The work is entirely in silico and has not yet been validated experimentally.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer under exposure to synthetic phenolic antioxidants: An integrated network toxicology and molecular docking approach.
papers.abstract: This study aims to investigate the multi-target molecular mechanisms through which synthetic phenolic antioxidants (SPAs) may contribute to colorectal cancer (CRC) progression using an integrated approach of network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. A representative library of traditional and novel SPAs was selected, and their toxicity profiles and carcinogenicity were predicted via ADMETlab 3.0. Potential targets of SPAs were retrieved from SwissTargetPrediction, SEA, PharmMapper, and ChEMBL. CRC-related targets were collected from GeneCards, TTD, and OMIM
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict how synthetic phenolic antioxidants (common food additives) might contribute to colorectal cancer. The authors built a library of these compounds, predicted their toxicity and carcinogenicity, and identified overlapping protein targets between the antioxidants and colorectal cancer. The work is entirely computational and proposes multi-target mechanisms rather than providing experimental validation.

papers.title: NOS2 as a candidate molecular link between air pollutants and depression: an integrated computational and experimental study.
papers.abstract: Studies exploring the molecules and potential mechanisms linking air pollution exposure to depression remain scarce. This study aimed to elucidate the potential regulatory molecules and possible mechanisms associated with air pollutants and depression, thereby providing scientific clues for disease prevention and treatment.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates computational analyses with experimental validation to identify NOS2 (inducible nitric oxide synthase) as a candidate molecular mediator linking air pollutant exposure to depression. The authors propose that pollutant-driven NOS2 regulation may contribute to depressive pathology, offering a potential target for prevention or treatment. The work is exploratory and provides preliminary mechanistic clues rather than definitive causal evidence.
